title: Signal fanout and staged shadow-eval lane for model catalog submissions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a mix of new model requests, version-pin requests, and deprecation notices. Current intake is a single queue with manual triage; this creates long turnaround for enterprise-sensitive requests and limited ability to run targeted shadow evaluations before pinning or deprecation.

Goal: Introduce a deterministic signal fanout at intake and a staged 'shadow-eval' lane that automatically routes eligible submissions to low-risk validation (shadow traffic, eval harnesses, compatibility tests) before enabling pin/deprecation actions. The flow should reduce time-to-decision for enterprise requests, produce deterministic evidence (eval metrics + compatibility checks), and provide an opt-in fastpath for sponsored customers.

Proposal summary:
1) Intake signal fanout: enrich submissions with structured signals (customer tier, requested action: add|pin|deprecate, model family, quantization, privacy requirements, requested SLA). Use these signals to route submissions into lanes: fastpath-review, staged-shadow-eval, and standard-triage.
2) Staged shadow-eval lane: for requests routed here, automatically trigger a lightweight shadow run using the submitting customer's representative prompt set (if provided) and Redwood canonical eval suites. Aggregate latency/cost/quality deltas and compatibility checks (APIs, tokenization, structured-output regressions).
3) Decision policy: surface a recommendation (approve | require more tests | reject) to PM/Model Steward. For pin/deprecate actions, require passing a minimal set of eval thresholds or an explicit sponsor approval.
4) Fastpath: sponsorship-based manual override to expedite approval (> SLA customers), but require mandatory post-approval monitoring and rollback hooks.
5) Observability & artifacts: store evaluation artifacts in catalog (links to logs, evaluation dashboards, diff reports) and surface in Console model detail page.

Trade-offs considered:
- Higher automation accelerates reviews but may miss nuanced product-specific regressions; mitigated by staged rollout and human-in-the-loop checks for P0/P1 customers.
- Running shadow evals increases infra cost; we'll cap per-request compute and rely on sampling for large model families.

Deliverables:
- Intake schema extension and routing rules (PM + ENG).
- Shadow evaluation harness and lightweight infra budget cap (ENG + Research).
- UI changes in Console for review recommendations and artifact links (Product + Design).
- Playbook for sponsors and support (Customer Success + Sales).
updates: 2025-02-12 | Asha Patel: Initial ticket created to capture recurring enterprise pain points with long model-catalog lead times. Draft proposal added.
2025-02-14 | Miguel Torres: Kickoff with ENG-Infra and Research; agreed to prototype routing via existing webhook fields. Action: ENG to surface required signals by 2025-02-21.

2025-02-17 | Research (Lena Choi): Ran exploratory shadow eval on three community models using representative prompt sets; observed consistent latency regressions when quantized variants differ. Need compatibility checks in harness.
2025-02-20 | PM Review: Confirmed acceptance criteria and added release target catalog-2.14. Requested design sketches for Console surfaces by 2025-02-25.
review_feedback: Design (Ravi Kapoor): Prefer a collapsible artifacts panel in model detail to avoid cluttering the existing UI. Suggested mock: small summary + link to full diffs.
Security (Marta Nguyen): Shadow runs must not retain unredacted customer data; require token obfuscation and KMS-scoped keys. Marked security_review_required.
Engineering (Priya Shah): Recommend staged rollout to 10% of catalog traffic first to validate infra cost models; propose budget cap per request to limit spend.
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema extended to include required routing signals and documented in Confluence
Routing engine can auto-classify submissions into three lanes with >= 90% precision on a sampled validation set
Shadow-eval harness runs end-to-end for a test submission and produces an artifacts bundle (latency, cost, quality diffs, compatibility checks) stored and linkable from the catalog UI
PM + Model Steward can act on recommendations and decision is recorded with artifact links
Fastpath sponsor override exists and enforces mandatory 7-day post-approval monitoring with automatic rollback trigger on regression (>5% quality delta)
Security sign-off obtained for data handling in shadow runs
